allowRule.statement: A row is allowed only if each of the five required dimensions is present and non-conflicting. The frozen section 4 acceptance bullet 1 requires the tool, model, version, distribution hash and license to be PRESENT, so for tool, version, distributionHash and license only state 'known' satisfies the rule. 'model' is the single applicability dimension: it is satisfied by 'known' (a concrete model identity) or by an explicit 'notApplicable' (the row is not a model host). A row with any dimension missing is blocked. A row whose license/model-id/hash/approver sources conflict is blocked AND registered as an unresolved SOURCE_CONFLICT; no value is selected silently.
allowRule.dimensionShape: all five dimensions have the same object shape {value, state, ...}. 'tool' was an untyped string in an earlier draft, so a predicate reading r['tool']['state'] was unevaluable on 19/19 rows; it is now an object on every row.

allowedStateVocabulary.rule: of the recorded tokens, only these satisfy /allowRule/allowedPredicate
allowedStateVocabulary.whySeparated: record vocabulary and allow vocabulary are deliberately different. An earlier draft accepted 'notApplicable' on version, distributionHash and license, which would have let a row with no version, no hash and no license be allowed; that contradicts frozen section 4 bullet 1 and the C01 negative case ('missing hash/license ... => blocked'). No row currently uses notApplicable on those three dimensions, so the defect was latent; the predicate is fixed so it cannot become live.

allowRule.allowedPredicate: for r in rows: r['status'] == 'allowed' iff r['tool']['state'] == 'known' AND r['model']['state'] in {'known','notApplicable'} AND r['version']['state'] == 'known' AND r['distributionHash']['state'] == 'known' AND r['license']['state'] == 'known' AND r['conflicts'] == [] AND r['conflictState'] is null AND r['approval']['owner'] is not null
allowRule.conflictRule: any dimension with conflicting sources => status 'blocked', conflictState 'unresolved', and a SOURCE_CONFLICT entry in /conflicts. The conflicting values are preserved side by side; neither is selected. The per-row key /allowlistRows[*].conflictState now carries 'unresolved' on a conflicting row and null on every other row, so the state this rule declares is actually present in the row set; /conflicts[*].resolution remains the authoritative statement of the resolution and the row key is a projection of it.
